cards.explanation: The answer is False. Eliphaz asks “Does He profit if your ways are blameless?” and I think the question is meant to have a no hiding in it (Job 22:3). He's saying God doesn't gain from Job's goodness. Eliphaz is a friend of Job's (Job 2:11), and he's leaning hard on that point.

The answer is his great wickedness. Eliphaz asks, “Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?” (Job 22:5). That's his answer to why Job is hurting. Notice he says it as a question, which is a very polite way to swing a hammer.

The answer is that he withheld water and food. Eliphaz says, “You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished…” (Job 22:7). Those are his words, and they're part of his list. Water for the thirsty, food for the hungry, and he says Job held both back.

The blanks are widows and fatherless. Eliphaz says, “You sent widows away empty-handed…” (Job 22:9). Widows are first on this part of the list, and I think this one hits hard to hear, even as an accusation. Then he says “…the strength of the fatherless was crushed.” (Job 22:9). The fatherless are children without a dad, and he says it as part of his charge against Job.

The answer is a flood of water. Eliphaz says, “…it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.” (Job 22:11). Dark and wet at the same time sounds like the worst power outage ever, friends. He's describing Job's trouble that way.

The answer is True. Eliphaz claims Job says, “What does God know?” (Job 22:13). He goes on with what he says Job says: “Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven.” (Job 22:14). Both lines are Eliphaz's claim about Job's words.

The answer is “Depart from us.” Eliphaz says the wicked men of old told God, “Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?” (Job 22:17). Those are the words he gives the wicked men of long ago. He says they were snatched away before their time (Job 22:16).

The answer is True. Eliphaz says, “But it was He who filled their houses with good things…” (Job 22:18). So the good things came from God, in his telling. He says it about the same men who told God, “Depart from us.” (Job 22:17).

The answer is glad. Eliphaz says, “The righteous see it and are glad…” (Job 22:19). That's how he pictures the righteous reacting when the wicked are destroyed. It's his picture, and he gives it in one short line.

The answer is in his heart. Eliphaz says, “Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.” (Job 22:22). Not just hear them, friends, but store them. Like keeping the good recipe where you can't lose it.

The answer is True. Eliphaz says, “If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored.” (Job 22:23). It's a promise with an “if” in front. He goes on to talk about removing injustice from Job's tents.

The answer is the Almighty Himself. Eliphaz says, “…then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.” (Job 22:25). Not a thing God gives, but God Himself. That's his offer after he talks about the gold of Ophir.
The answer is False. Eliphaz says, “You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.” (Job 22:27). God hears, according to him. That's part of his picture of a comeback.
The answer is light. Eliphaz says, “…light will shine on your ways.” (Job 22:28). Earlier he said it was so dark Job could not see (Job 22:11). Now he promises the opposite.

The answer is even one who is not innocent. Eliphaz says, “He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.” (Job 22:30). That's the last line he speaks in this passage. The rescue comes through Job's clean hands, he says.
